Benfica began as a country village. In the 15th century, it was made a Lisbon judicial district with two private judges. Three brotherhoods also settled here at the same time: Nossa Senhora do Amparo, Santo António and São Sebastião. When the Lisbon judicial district was abolished in 1852, Benfica became part of the new municipality of Belém, and then in 1886 it was split off. The part outside the new Lisbon ring road became part of Oeiras (and now Amadora), while the part inside joined Lisbon, giving rise to the current parish. The city continued to grow, which is reflected in the increasing urbanisation of the parish. The population tripled from 17,843 to around 50,000 between the 1950s and the 1990s. The territory was divided again in 1959 with the creation of the São Domingos de Benfica parish. More recently, although there are more buildings, the resident population is shrinking because of ageing and the migration of the younger inhabitants to the periphery. José, Coração de Jesus and São Mamede. This group of parishes stems from the administrative reorganisation of the city of Lisbon, which took place in September 2013. The history of these parishes goes much further back. At the end of the 12th century, under the authority of the Bishop of Lisbon, the first ten parishes appeared in the capital (delimited areas, in the city or the countryside, where individuals who followed the same religion lived, and their focal point was the temple or the mother church). In 1247, São Mamede was born, famous for housing the Lisbon Botanical Garden and the National Press Building. It is the oldest of the parishes that today make up Santo António. In the 16th century, Lisbon's Jewish and Moorish communities were extinct. At the same time, conquests, shipping and maritime trade brought more wealth to the kingdom. An increase in the population created the need for more parishes. Twelve new parishes appeared like this in November 1567. Among them is the parish of S. José, which is renowned for places like Parque Mayer, Avenida da Liberdade and Cinema Tivoli. The 1755 earthquake caused the destruction and collapse of many houses and buildings in Lisbon. Once again, the city needed to be redistributed and reorganised. Therefore, among two others, the parish of Sta. Joana appeared - later it was called Coração de Jesus (Heart of Jesus), covering the area of Marquês do Pombal and Avenida da Liberdade. A prestigious location that reflects the added value of living in the city centre and enjoying a city life where everything needed for daily comfort is close at hand. Nearby we can find lots of transport, supermarkets, heritage (Aqueduto das Águas Livres, former Colégio dos Nobres, Casa de Almeida Negreiros, Chafariz do Rato), churches (Igreja de S. Mamede, Igreja do Convento de Santo António dos Capuchos), gardens (Botanical Garden of the University of Lisbon, Mãe de Água das Amoreiras), Palaces (Palácio dos Marqueses da Praia, Rebelo de Andrade-Seia Palace, Dukes of Palmela Palace, Castilho Palace), theatres (Maria Vitória Theatre, Tivoli Theatre, Mayer Park), the São Jorge Cinema, Cinemateca Portuguesa, as well as various restaurants, traditional and luxury shops.
